subject: Analytics sourcing playbook — consultant shortlist + licensing approach
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Analytics sourcing playbook — consultant shortlist + licensing approach

Team —

Following our pricing review last week, I pulled an initial vendor scorecard and a proposed timeline for procurement (attached). High-level ask: we need a shortlist of 2 consulting partners and a recommendation for licensing (Snowflake reserved vs BigQuery flex + Metabase vs Looker) to present to finance on Nov 25.

Notes from discovery:
- Cost sensitivity for tokenized usage is high — prefer predictable reserved commits where possible.
- A lightweight BI layer is acceptable as long as we can keep dev ops overhead low.

Attachments: vendor_scorecard.xlsx, procurement_timeline.pdf

Can each of you add 1-2 names for consulting partners and any hard constraints (SLA, data residency) by EOD Nov 5? I can take vendor outreach and schedule discovery demos next week.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Analytics sourcing playbook — consultant shortlist + licensing approach

Ben —

Thanks for kicking this off. A few quick constraints from my side:
- We need the vendor to support private deployment patterns (VPC/on-prem connectors) for a subset of regulated customers.
- Preference for consultants with prior experience migrating Looker -> Metabase migrations (we have 120+ dashboards).
- Target budget for consulting: not to exceed $260k for phase 1 (discovery + migration plan).

Candidates I recommend: DataCraft Partners (has SSO/KMS experience), and Harbor Analytics (smaller boutique, fast execution). Monica — can you pull their 2025 references?

Also looping in Sam Park from Metabase (external) to get a preliminary licensing quote — Sam, would you be able to share typical pricing bands for a company our size and any migration assistance you offer?

Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Platform Strategy — Redwood Inference
From: Sam Park <sam@metabasepro.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T15:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Analytics sourcing playbook — consultant shortlist + licensing approach

On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 10:04 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Also looping in Sam Park from Metabase (external) to get a preliminary licensing quote — Sam, would you be able to share typical pricing bands for a company our size and any migration assistance you offer?

Hi Mina & team —

Appreciate the intro. Quick summary from Metabase Solutions:
- Licensing: three tiers (Starter, Business, Enterprise). For orgs with ~150 engineers + prods we typically recommend Business or Enterprise; rough ballpark $30k-$90k/yr depending on data connectors and SSO/KMS requirements.
- Migration: we offer a migration add-on ($25k-$60k) that covers dashboard translation, QA, and a 2-week knowledge transfer.
- Private deployment: supported (self-hosted or VPC).

I can send a formal pricing PDF and availability for a 45-minute demo next Tue/Thu. Attaching a short product brief in this thread.

Best,
Sam Park
Senior Solutions Engineer — Metabase Solutions
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataCraft Partners <procurement@datacraft.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Analytics sourcing playbook — consultant shortlist + licensing approach

Team —

I pulled cost estimates for the options discussed. Attached a quick CSV comparing Looker migration vs Metabase adoption (cost_estimate_looker_vs_metabase.csv). Key takeaways:
- Snowflake reserved capacity + Looker managed is the highest TCO (30% higher Y1) but lowest dev overhead.
- BigQuery + Metabase is 20% lower Y1 but frontloads consulting and integration work.

I also reached out to DataCraft Partners for an SOW draft; they returned an initial SOW (datacraft_sow_v1.pdf) that fits the $200–260k band for phase 1. I requested references and SOC2 evidence; they replied they have SOC2 Type II in place.

Action items:
- Ben: schedule vendor demos (Sam + Snowflake + DataCraft) for week of Nov 15.
- Mina: I'll draft a short decision matrix for the Nov 25 finance readout.

Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Procurement Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Analytics sourcing playbook — consultant shortlist + licensing approach

Quick executive summary to add to the packet:

- Goal: reduce end-to-end analytics latency for product signals by 25% and cut monthly infra spend on analytics by 15% within 12 months.
- Recommendation (prelim): pursue BigQuery + Metabase path with DataCraft for phase 1 assessment, conditional on DataCraft references and SOC2 review. This path best balances cost and operational control.
- Risk: migration effort may touch ~40 dashboards with custom SQL/explores; need two weeks of freeze/QA per workspace.

Please prepare a one-pager (1 slide + 1 page memo) by Nov 23 so I can consolidate for the Nov 25 finance meeting (decision authority: CFO & Head of Platform).

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP Product — Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, DataCraft Partners <procurement@datacraft.com>, Sam Park <sam@metabasepro.com>, Snowflake Sales <snow-sales@snowflake.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Analytics sourcing playbook — consultant shortlist + licensing approach

Team + vendors —

Thank you for the quick turnaround. After reviewing Monica's cost matrix and Lauren's summary, leadership is comfortable moving forward with a formal RFP and procurement for phase 1 on the BigQuery + Metabase path, pending:
1) DataCraft references + SOC2 evidence (Monica — please confirm receipt and share by EOD Nov 23).
2) Metabase formal licensing PDF and migration SOW (Sam — please upload to the Drive link listed below).
3) Snowflake to provide a counterproposal (we want a data point on reserved capacity scenarios).

Next steps I am assigning:
- Monica: own the RFP issuance and vendor evaluation (scorecard will be the canonical doc).
- Ben: schedule vendor demos and collect follow-up pricing.
- Lauren: compile the 1-pager for finance.
- Mina: finalize procurement timeline and present at the Nov 25 readout.
